re_line: Australia-Philippines defence pact signed at ASEAN · US unveils $450M COFA grants for Palau, FSM, Marshall Islands · Albanese leaves door open to Putin APEC photo · Albanese apologizes for COP31 hot-mic · AUKUS inquiry flags $180B waste bill
morning_memo: Canberra and Manila signed a new defence and intelligence cooperation pact on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit, deepening ties as China asserts authority in the South China Sea.

Washington approved more than $450 million in Compact of Free Association assistance for Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, and the Marshall Islands, tying the funds to countering Chinese influence among the freely associated states.
Albanese apologized for a hot-mic exchange with Chris Bowen caught at COP31, even as he left open the possibility of appearing in an APEC photo alongside Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen this week.

top_stories.headline: Australia and Philippines sign new defence pact at ASEAN summit
top_stories.body: Australia and the Philippines signed a new defence and intelligence cooperation agreement in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit, deepening military ties as China asserts authority in the South China Sea. Foreign Minister **Penny Wong**'s department said the pact would enhance "defence cooperation and maritime security" across Southeast Asia. The agreement expands intelligence sharing between Canberra and Manila as Beijing pushes its claims across contested waters.
top_stories.src_line: per SMH (Natassia Chrysanthos): "Drones, intelligence and a bucket of chicken: Australia and the Philippines sign new defence pact" · also Reuters, Bloomberg

top_stories.headline: US approves $450 million in COFA grants for three Pacific compact states
top_stories.body: The U.S. Department of the Interior announced more than *$450 million* in Compact of Free Association economic assistance for Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, and the Marshall Islands, following September's JEMCO and JEMFAC committee meetings. An Interior official said the funding reflects the administration's commitment to "countering malign influence in the Pacific" while ensuring taxpayer dollars are used responsibly. The three states are among the Pacific's freely associated states under compacts with Washington.
top_stories.src_line: per Pacific Island Times: "US announces $450M in COFA grants for Palau, FSM and Marshall Islands"

top_stories.headline: Albanese won't rule out APEC photo with Putin
top_stories.body: **Anthony Albanese** left open the possibility of appearing in an APEC leaders' family photo alongside Vladimir Putin in China this week, saying he would "respect and...take into consideration the wishes of our host country." Canada's Mark Carney has indicated he would join the photo out of respect for Beijing. Albanese is in Manila for the ASEAN summit before traveling to Shenzhen and has welcomed proposed Trump-Xi-Putin talks despite Ukrainian objections.
top_stories.src_line: per ABC News: "Albanese stands by Ukraine but won't rule out photo with Putin" · also Guardian Australia, AFR

overnight_items.headline: US Democrat urges AI access for Five Eyes partners like Australia
overnight_items.body_text: A leading U.S. Democrat said Five Eyes intelligence partners including Australia should not be denied access to the most powerful American AI models, after one such tool was withheld from Australian users. The intervention adds a new front to alliance technology-sharing debates alongside AUKUS Pillar 2 cooperation.

overnight_items.headline: Chinese state media questions 'Squad' prospects after AU-Philippines pact
overnight_items.body_text: Global Times reported on the new Australia-Philippines defence pact signed amid South China Sea tensions, citing an expert who questioned the durability of the informal "Squad" security grouping. The state-run outlet framed the agreement as part of a broader U.S.-aligned effort to contain China in the region.

overnight_items.headline: Defence reverses Victoria Barracks sale plan, sparking upkeep questions
overnight_items.body_text: The federal government has walked back its February plan to sell Sydney's Victoria Barracks, Australia's oldest active military site in use since 1848, after public backlash drew crowds of more than 100 to its weekly tours. The reversal leaves open questions about long-term upkeep of the heritage defence property.

overnight_items.headline: Fiji party says constitutional reform must benefit citizens, not politicians
overnight_items.body_text: We Unite Fiji told the Constitution Amendment Bill Special Committee that proposed reforms must serve ordinary Fijians rather than political interests, joining other parties scrutinizing the bill. The submission follows separate warnings from Next Gen against removing the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption without a strong replacement.

aukus_watch.headline: US Ambassador tours AUKUS submarine on first WA visit
aukus_watch.body_text: U.S. Ambassador to Australia **David Brat** toured an AUKUS submarine during his first visit to Western Australia, home to HMAS Stirling. The visit marks continued high-level U.S. engagement with the submarine program's build-out in the state.

pacific_wire.headline: Pacific fuel crisis cost region nearly $1 billion in six months
pacific_wire.body_text: Officials briefing New Zealand said the fuel crisis triggered by the Iran-U.S. war in late February cost the Pacific region nearly *$1 billion* in its first six months. The figure underscores the economic strain facing import-dependent island economies from a conflict thousands of kilometers away.

pacific_wire.headline: Small Island states get just 3% of climate finance despite $100B goal
pacific_wire.body_text: **Tabuya** said Small Island Developing States receive only *3 percent* of global climate finance despite the world's $100 billion annual finance goal being met, days before COP31 concludes in Antalya. The gap leaves Pacific nations exposed to climate impacts without matching resources to adapt.

pacific_wire.headline: UN launches $3 billion disaster risk financing platform at COP31
pacific_wire.body_text: The United Nations launched a Disaster Risk Financing Platform at COP31 in Antalya aiming to secure access to more than *$3 billion* in risk financing to protect 75 million people from climate shocks by 2030. The initiative is designed to make humanitarian responses faster and more predictable for vulnerable states including Pacific nations.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji party opposes removing anti-corruption body without replacement
pacific_wire.body_text: Fiji's Next Gen party told the Constitution Amendment Bill Special Committee that the Fiji Independent Commission Against Corruption should be retained, warning its removal without a strong replacement could weaken anti-corruption efforts. Member **Samisoni Ralulu** said the party acknowledges concerns about FICAC's recent performance but opposes scrapping it outright.

pacific_wire.headline: Fiji police say no special recruitment needed for elections, referendum
pacific_wire.body_text: Fiji police said they are prepared for upcoming elections and a referendum without requiring special recruitment, as the country's electoral and constitutional reform process continues. The assurance comes amid separate civil society warnings about risks in proposed centralized vote counting.

pacific_wire.headline: Vanuatu cooperative exports over 14 tonnes of taro to New Zealand
pacific_wire.body_text: The Vanuatu Cooperative Business Network exported more than *14 tonnes* of fresh taro to New Zealand, opening new market access for farmers in Tanna. The shipment strengthens Vanuatu's agricultural export trade and diversifies income sources for rural producers.

new_zealand.headline: Legal scholar calls New Zealand's constitution 'unjust' and outdated
new_zealand.body_text: Professor **Claire Charters** told RNZ that New Zealand's uncodified constitution is unusual internationally and fails to adequately reflect Maori rights, calling for fundamental legal change in her new book. She said courts' inability to overturn legislation inconsistent with fundamental rights remains a distinctive and contested feature of New Zealand law.

new_zealand.headline: NZ First still weighs MP Michael Laws' future in the party
new_zealand.body_text: **Winston Peters** said NZ First is still considering MP Michael Laws' position in the party, with further consequences possible once NZ First has time to meet after the election. The review follows prior concerns Peters had flagged about Laws.

new_zealand.headline: Atlas Network founder seeks New Zealand recruits for low-cost lobbying
new_zealand.body_text: A British think tank pioneer linked to the Atlas Network is courting New Zealand backers, including a prominent brewing figure, for low-cost political influence efforts that stop short of direct political action. The approach reflects growing international interest in New Zealand as a target for free-market advocacy networks.

canberra_politics.headline: Albanese apologises for hot-mic exchange with Bowen at COP31
canberra_politics.body_text: Anthony Albanese apologised after he and Energy Minister **Chris Bowen** were caught on a hot microphone joking about mobile phones and radiation at the COP31 climate talks, an exchange the Coalition branded "locker-room talk." Albanese said during a visit to HMAS Stalwart in the Philippines that "I of course regret that. I apologise."

canberra_politics.headline: Lambie urges means-testing of childcare and EV subsidies
canberra_politics.body_text: Independent senator **Jacqui Lambie** called on the government to means-test subsidies including child care, using a couple earning $500,000 combined as an example of poor targeting. She also urged "courage" to consider a new gas export tax, as Treasurer Jim Chalmers faces pressure to find savings ahead of December's budget update.

canberra_politics.headline: Katherine Deves to run for One Nation in NSW upper house
canberra_politics.body_text: Former federal Liberal candidate **Katherine Deves**, known for campaigning to exclude transgender women from women's sport, will stand for One Nation at next year's New South Wales election. NSW One Nation leader Mike Newman said Deves and three other candidates were "people from the real world," not career politicians.

canberra_politics.headline: Liberal senator warns against sacrificing artists for AI investment
canberra_politics.body_text: Liberal senator **Andrew McLachlan** said artists' copyright must not be "sacrificed" to attract AI investment, and new data centres should not be prioritised over environmental concerns. His intervention adds to intra-Coalition friction as Labor weighs copyright changes within a broader AI policy package covering data centres, online safety and energy.

canberra_politics.headline: Ombudsman warns of more social media lockouts under duty-of-care laws
canberra_politics.body_text: The telecommunications industry ombudsman warned big tech firms may shut down more user accounts as Australia's digital duty-of-care laws approach, with no independent umpire yet available for affected Australians. The warning adds pressure on the government as it finalises the regulatory regime.

business_economy.headline: Australia auction clearances slump to six-year low as rates rise
business_economy.body_text: Capital city auction clearance rates fell to their lowest level in six years as higher interest rates and weaker buyer demand weigh on the property market, Bloomberg reported. The slide adds pressure on the Reserve Bank, which held its cash rate at 4.35 percent on November 11 after three increases earlier in the year.

business_economy.headline: Fiji Stock Exchange marks 30 years as airport needs $2.3 billion
business_economy.body_text: Fiji Airports chief executive **Mesake Nawari**, honored with the South Pacific Stock Exchange's Lifetime Achievement Award, said Fiji Airports must raise *$2.3 billion* to fund airport development and will explore capital market instruments including green and blue bonds. Nawari, who helped launch the exchange in 1996 with four listed companies, said foreign investors remain key to its growth.

primary_documents.headline: Enhancing defence cooperation and maritime security in Southeast Asia
primary_documents.body_text: Foreign Minister Penny Wong's office issued a release on enhancing defence cooperation and maritime security in Southeast Asia, coinciding with the signing of Australia's new defence pact with the Philippines at the ASEAN summit.

calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Decides the government of Australia's second-largest state, with One Nation and independent challengers testing major-party dominance ahead of the next federal contest.

calendar_watch.event: Australian Senate vote on gas reservation bill
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Passage is uncertain without Greens or Coalition support, shaping domestic gas supply and export policy.
Albanese faces a decision on joining a leaders' photo that may include Vladimir Putin, testing Australia's balancing act between Beijing ties and support for Ukraine.

calendar_watch.event: COP31 climate negotiations conclude in Antalya
calendar_watch.why_it_matters: Outcomes on loss-and-damage financing and emissions commitments directly affect Pacific Island states' climate diplomacy demands on Australia.

key_stat.label: US COFA economic assistance for Palau, FSM, Marshall Islands
key_stat.context: Interior Department grants approved after September's JEMCO and JEMFAC meetings aim to deepen security ties and counter Chinese influence among the three freely associated states.

also_today.headline: Young voters, 44% of the roll, loom large in Victorian election
also_today.body_text: ABC reporting found voters aged 18 to 44 will make up 44 percent of the vote in the November 28 Victorian election, according to the Victorian Electoral Commission, with many regional youths turning to alternative parties amid dissatisfaction with major parties.

also_today.headline: Book argues federal government complicit in NT policy failures
also_today.body_text: A new book by veteran journalist **Murray McLaughlin**, "The Northern Territory: A Litany of Failure," argues Canberra has been "passively complicit" in worsening outcomes for Aboriginal Territorians since self-government in 1978. McLaughlin, a former adviser to the Northern Land Council, says the Territory "will never right itself" without direct Commonwealth intervention.

also_today.headline: Albanese caught between climate ambition and political reality at COP31
also_today.body_text: Australia is using COP31 to position itself as a Pacific climate leader, with Anthony Albanese telling the Antalya summit that nations like Tuvalu face an "existential threat," though delegates offered a muted reception. The Coalition has criticized the summit's cost domestically, exposing what ABC described as contradictions between Australia's climate ambitions abroad and political reality at home.
